Model – Types (Cont.)

   – Agent-Based Modeling (ABM): focuses on autonomous software "agents" that interact
        with each other and their environment based on specific rules to achieve goals.
             • A key feature is autonomy; agents act in their own interest without centralized control,
           making this paradigm ideal for studying social and human phenomena.
             •  This is the primary paradigm for Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) in AI, where multiple robots
           must coordinate in a warehouse without a central controller.
   – Aggregate Modeling: This method combines smaller objects and actions into a single
         representation to improve performance or handle large scales.
             •  These are typically constructive models rather than physics-based.
   – Hybrid Modeling: Combining multiple modeling paradigms into
        a single simulation.
             •  Combining paradigms, such as using physics-based modeling
               for a robot's movement while using agent-based modeling for
                  its social interactions with humans
